title: Scalar restriction and composition for normalized bar maps
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category and $R$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$; it is the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the constant ring on the topology generated by singleton identities [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Derived categories and cochain complexes mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here left $V$-acyclic means that the canonical comparison $LV(M[0])\to V(M)[0]$ is an isomorphism for the object $M$ in question. For $U\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-module $M$, put $L_U(M)(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}M$, with restriction along $b:W\to V$ sending $(a,m)$ to $(ab,m)$. For $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$, let $B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}L_{U_n}(F(U_0))$ for $n\ge0$, with zero positive terms. On evaluation at $V$ its generators are $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. The face $d_j$ deletes $U_{n-j}$, composing adjacent arrows (including $a$ when $j=0$); the last face restricts $x$ along $U_1\to U_0$. Use differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ for $n>0$, and augmentation $a_F(a:V\to U_0,x)=F(a)x$ in degree zero. Put $C_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ deleting $U_{n-j}$, composing at internal vertices and restricting the coefficient only for $j=n$. Let $\rho:R\to S$ be any homomorphism of commutative rings and $H\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,S}$. Restriction $\operatorname{Res}_\rho$ regards an $S$-module as an $R$-module via $r\cdot x=\rho(r)x$, without changing its underlying abelian group or maps. There are natural isomorphisms of augmented presheaf complexes $B_{\mathcal E,R}(\operatorname{Res}_\rho H)\cong\operatorname{Res}_\rho B_{\mathcal E,S}(H)$ and of complexes $K_{\mathcal E,R}(\operatorname{Res}_\rho H)\cong\operatorname{Res}_\rho K_{\mathcal E,S}(H)$, identity on coefficients of generators. Suppose these augmentations and their termwise acyclicity give the canonical comparisons $m=Q(b)\varepsilon_B LC(Qa)^{-1}$ to the total derived colimits (defined everywhere [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]). The displayed isomorphisms induce a canonical isomorphism in $D(R)$,
$$LC_{\mathcal E,R}(\operatorname{Res}_\rho H[0])\cong\operatorname{Res}_\rho LC_{\mathcal E,S}(H[0]),$$
whose conjugate by the two $m$'s is precisely the displayed isomorphism of $K$-complexes. For small $\mathcal D$, $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$ and semilinear natural $t:F\to u^{-1}G$ with $G\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal D,S}$, the maps $(U_\bullet,x)\mapsto(uU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$ factor through the same-ring map to $K_{\mathcal D,R}(\operatorname{Res}_\rho G)$ and the scalar-restriction isomorphism. For composable $(u,\rho,t)$ and $(v,\sigma,s)$, their composite is exactly the chain map $(U_\bullet,x)\mapsto(vuU_\bullet,s_{uU_0}t_{U_0}x)$ for $(vu,\sigma\rho,st)$, under the usual iterated scalar-restriction identification; identity data give the identity chain map. These identities persist under the normalized derived comparisons. Restriction is exact and preserves the cone roofs for connecting maps. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ or preservation of projectives by restriction is assumed.

proof.text: Write $r=\operatorname{Res}_\rho$, both on modules and objectwise on presheaves. Since $r$ changes neither abelian groups nor maps, kernels, images and cokernels are the same groups with the restricted action. Thus $r$ is additive and exact, and $H^i(rX)=rH^i(X)$ for every complex $X$: both sides are the same kernel modulo the same image. In particular $r$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. For every family $(M_j)$ of $S$-modules, the finite-support description identifies $\bigoplus_j rM_j$ with $r(\bigoplus_jM_j)$ by $(j,x)\mapsto(j,x)$; addition and the $R$-action agree on both sides. These arguments apply without a flatness assumption.

The complexes and augmentation are well-defined by [lem-trf-augmented-presheaf-bar-resolution], which states the face identities and the coefficientwise colimit identification $b$. Apply the finite-support identification of Step 1 to both sums in each term of $B$, and to the sum in each term of $K$. Denote the resulting maps by $\beta_H:B_R(rH)\to rB_S(H)$ and $\kappa_H:K_R(rH)\to rK_S(H)$. Their inverses keep every coefficient and index unchanged. Presheaf restriction changes $(a,x)$ to $(ab,x)$ on both sides, so $\beta_H$ is a presheaf map. Each face with $j<n$ changes only an index or composes arrows, and the last face applies the same additive restriction map of $H$ on both sides. Consequently these maps commute with every face, hence with the signed differential. Also $r(a_H)\beta_H=a_{rH}$, since both send $(a,x)$ to $H(a)x$. The same checks with a map $H\to H^{\prime}$ establish naturality. All sums are small since $\mathcal E$ is small.

By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], the exact functor $r$ of Step 1 induces the termwise functor $Dr:D(S)\to D(R)$ (and similarly for presheaves). Use its localization identification $Dr(QX)\cong Q(rX)$ throughout. The hypothesis supplies the normalized isomorphisms $m_R:LC_R(rH[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QK_R(rH)$ and $m_S:LC_S(H[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QK_S(H)$. Define
$$\alpha_H=(Dr(m_S))^{-1}\circ Q(\kappa_H)\circ m_R.$$
Then $Dr(m_S)\alpha_H=Q(\kappa_H)m_R$, and invertibility of $Dr(m_S)$ makes this the unique isomorphism with the required normalization. For $h:H\to H'$, naturality of the augmentation $a$, the colimit identification $b$, and the derived comparison $\varepsilon$ in the assumed formula for $m$ gives $m_{H'}LC(h)=QK(h)m_H$: substitute their naturality equations into $m=Q(b)\varepsilon_BLC(Qa)^{-1}$. Combine this equation over $R$ and over $S$ with $Q(rK(h))Q(\kappa_H)=Q(\kappa_{H'})QK(rh)$ from Step 2. Substitution in the displayed formula for $\alpha$ gives $Dr(LC_S(h))\alpha_H=\alpha_{H'}LC_R(rh)$, proving naturality. No preservation of projective resolutions is required.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), exact functor localization; the alpha formula is the agent normalization calculation using the m hypothesis

proof.text: For semilinear $t$, regard $t_U:F(U)\to rG(uU)$ as an $R$-linear map: $t_U(ax)=\rho(a)t_U(x)$ is exactly this linearity condition. Let $T_{u,t}$ be the same-ring map sending $(U_\bullet,x)$ to $(uU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$ in $K_{\mathcal D,R}(rG)$. Finite support makes this a well-defined map of direct sums even if $u$ identifies chains: the coefficients of coincident target chains are added. For $j<n$ the face equality is functoriality of $u$ and equality of unchanged coefficients. For the last face, for $f:U_1\to U_0$, the equality is $G(uf)t_{U_0}(x)=t_{U_1}(F(f)x)$, the naturality of $t$. Thus $T_{u,t}$ is a chain map. Composing it with $\kappa_G$ gives exactly the claimed semilinear formula into $rK_{\mathcal D,S}(G)$; this proves the stated factorization.

Let $\sigma:S\to T$ and $s:G\to v^{-1}J$ be the second datum. On every coefficient $x$, the composite sends $(U_\bullet,x)$ first to $(uU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$ and then to $(vuU_\bullet,s_{uU_0}t_{U_0}x)$. It is $\sigma\rho$-semilinear since $s(t(ax))=\sigma(\rho(a))s(t(x))$. The iterated restriction identification is the identity on underlying groups, because the two $R$-actions are both $a\cdot z=\sigma(\rho(a))z$. These facts identify the composite with the single map for $(vu,\sigma\rho,st)$ on every summand, hence on the whole direct sum; merging summands still gives the same finite sum. Identity data leave the chain and coefficient fixed. Likewise $\kappa_{\sigma\rho}=r_\rho(\kappa_\sigma)\kappa_\rho$ and the corresponding $\beta$ identity hold on every coefficient.

Use the localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the termwise restriction identifications of Step 3 understood. For a chain map $T_1:K_R(F)\to r_\rho K_S(G)$ its normalized derived map is $A_1=(Dr_\rho m_G)^{-1}Q(T_1)m_F$. For $T_2:K_S(G)\to r_\sigma K_T(J)$ write $A_2=(Dr_\sigma m_J)^{-1}Q(T_2)m_G$. Functoriality and inverse cancellation give
$$Dr_\rho(A_2)A_1=(Dr_\rho Dr_\sigma m_J)^{-1}Q(r_\rho T_2\circ T_1)m_F.$$
Indeed the middle factors are $Dr_\rho(m_G)Dr_\rho(m_G)^{-1}=1$. Step 5 identifies $r_\rho T_2\circ T_1$ with the single chain map for $(vu,\sigma\rho,st)$, and identifies iterated restriction with restriction along $\sigma\rho$. Thus the right side is precisely its normalized derived map. Identity data give $m_F^{-1}Q(1)m_F=1$. Taking $T_1=\kappa_\rho$ and $T_2=\kappa_\sigma$, with $F=r_\rho r_\sigma J$ and $G=r_\sigma J$, gives $Dr_\rho(\alpha_{\sigma,J})\alpha_{\rho,r_\sigma J}=\alpha_{\sigma\rho,J}$. This is the claimed scalar coherence as well as the general composition identity.

Finally take any cone roof for a connecting morphism, written $C\xleftarrow{q}\operatorname{Cone}(i)\xrightarrow{-\operatorname{pr}}A[1]$, where $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. With the convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $\operatorname{Cone}(i)^n=B^n\oplus A^{n+1}$ and $d(b,a)=(d_Bb+i(a),-d_Aa)$. Restriction gives the same direct sum, differential, projection and shift, identifying $r\operatorname{Cone}(i)$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(ri)$ and retaining the minus sign in the right arrow. Step 1 shows $rq$ is still a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $Dr$ sends the connecting roof to $rC\xleftarrow{rq}\operatorname{Cone}(ri)\xrightarrow{-\operatorname{pr}}rA[1]$, the corresponding roof after restriction. For a morphism of the sequences, the cone map $(b,a)\mapsto(f_Bb,f_Aa)$ is also unchanged. This proves preservation of these roofs and their commutative squares; no preservation of projectives is used.
